What do I need to use the calculator?

Two measurements: a snug underbust, taken level around the ribcage directly under the bust, and a loose bust measurement across the fullest point with the tape resting, not pulled. Inches or centimetres both work. The calculator turns the underbust into the band and the bust-band difference into the cup.

Which sizing systems does it return?

Brasize.ai returns US, UK, EU, AU and FR sizes, each with band, cup, full size and sister sizes. Showing the same size in every system a shopper will meet means an online order from a foreign brand lands right. The converter also handles cup ladders that diverge above D.

What is a sister size?

A sister size has the same cup volume on a different band. A 34C, 32D and 36B hold roughly the same volume, so going down a band and up a cup keeps the volume the same. Shoppers use sister sizes when a band runs tight or loose in a particular brand.

Why doesn't it add four inches to the band?

chunks.title: DueDateCalculator.ai Due Date Calculator
chunks.heading: DueDateCalculator.ai Due Date Calculator > The math, stated plainly
chunks.text:
Every NativeCode product publishes its assumptions on the page. This is the sequence the engine follows.

1. 01

 From the last period

 EDD = LMP + 280 days

 The standard convention. It assumes a 28-day cycle with ovulation near day 14; a different cycle length shifts the estimate by the difference from 28.

2. 02

 From conception

 EDD = conception + 266 days

 Two weeks fewer than the LMP count, which is why 40 weeks from the last period is roughly 38 weeks of development.

3. 03

 From IVF transfer

 EDD = transfer + 266 − embryo age

 A day-5 blastocyst is transfer + 261 days. Because the embryo's age is known exactly, this is the most precise self-calculation available.

4. 04

 Confirmed by ultrasound

 A first-trimester crown-rump measurement is the most accurate dating method. When it disagrees significantly with LMP dating, clinicians rely on the ultrasound, and only a clinician sets the official date.

What PeriodCalculator.ai is: PeriodCalculator.ai takes three inputs (first day of the last period, average cycle length, and period length) and returns a calibrated forecast: next period, ovulation, fertile window, and the current cycle phase, drawn on a dial rather than dumped in a table.

The math is stated plainly on the page. Ovulation is estimated as the projected next period minus the luteal phase, because the luteal phase is far steadier than the cycle itself. The luteal length is adjustable for people who have confirmed theirs with ovulation tests.

chunks.title: PeriodCalculator.ai Ovulation Calculator
chunks.heading: PeriodCalculator.ai Ovulation Calculator > The math, stated plainly
chunks.text:
Every NativeCode product publishes its assumptions on the page. This is the sequence the engine follows.

1. 01

 Project the next period

 next period = last period + cycle length

 A cycle is counted from the first day of bleeding to the day before the next bleed. The site projects three cycles, not one.

2. 02

 Count back to ovulation

 ovulation = next period − luteal phase

 The luteal phase holds near 14 days for most people while the follicular phase absorbs the variation, so counting backward is more reliable than the day-14 rule.

3. 03

 Bracket the fertile window

 window = 5 days before ovulation + ovulation day

 Sperm survive up to five days; the egg about one. Conception is likeliest in the final two days.

4. 04

 Calibrate to real data

 In an analysis of more than 600,000 cycles, only a minority were exactly 28 days. Entering real averages instead of defaults is what narrows the window.

With regular cycles, predictions are typically within a day or two. With irregular cycles, the site tells you to read each date as the center of a window. Entering your real average cycle and period length instead of the defaults is what narrows the window, since few cycles are exactly 28 days.

What TDEE.co is: TDEE.co answers the question behind every diet and training plan: how many calories do I actually burn in a day? It estimates basal metabolic rate with the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, switches to Katch-McArdle when a body-fat percentage is supplied, and multiplies by an honest activity factor between 1.2 and 1.9.

Every number the site produces lives on the same axis (resting burn, activity energy, the maintenance line, a goal deficit or surplus, and a macro split), so a visitor can see how one result becomes the next rather than juggling seven unrelated calculators.

chunks.title: TDEE.co TDEE, BMR and Macro Calculator
chunks.heading: TDEE.co TDEE, BMR and Macro Calculator > The math, stated plainly
chunks.text:
Every NativeCode product publishes its assumptions on the page. This is the sequence the engine follows.

1. 01

 Estimate resting burn

 BMR = 10·kg + 6.25·cm − 5·age + 5 (men) / − 161 (women)

 Mifflin-St Jeor is the default, recognised by the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics as the most accurate general-population equation.

2. 02

 Scale by activity

 TDEE = BMR × 1.2 … 1.9

 The multiplier is the single biggest variable. The site tells people to match an average week, not a best one. A desk job plus four hard sessions is ×1.55.

3. 03

 Refine with body fat

 BMR = 370 + 21.6 × lean mass (kg)

 Entering a body-fat percentage switches the engine to Katch-McArdle, which is driven by lean mass rather than total weight.

4. 04

 Steer to a goal

 −500 → ~1 lb/wk · +250 → lean gain

 Deficits and surpluses are applied to the maintenance line, with a low-calorie warning threshold of about 1,200 (women) and 1,500 (men).

What does TDEE.co calculate?

It calculates total daily energy expenditure, the calories you burn in a day, plus your BMR, calorie targets for losing, maintaining or gaining weight, and a suggested macro split. Every number sits on the same energy axis, so you can see how one result becomes the next.

Which formula does it use?

Mifflin-St Jeor by default, which the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics recognises as the most accurate general-population equation. If you enter a body-fat percentage, it switches to Katch-McArdle, which uses lean body mass. The result is then multiplied by an activity factor between 1.2 and 1.9.

How accurate is the result?

Typically within 5 to 10 percent of true daily burn. No formula can see genetics, hormones, sleep, stress or everyday movement, so the site recommends holding the target for two to three weeks, then adjusting by 100 to 200 calories against your weight trend.

chunks.title: TimeCalculator.ai Time and Date Calculator
chunks.heading: TimeCalculator.ai Time and Date Calculator > The math, stated plainly
chunks.text:
Every NativeCode product publishes its assumptions on the page. This is the sequence the engine follows.

1. 01

 Normalise to seconds

 t = h·3600 + m·60 + s

 Every clock time is converted to total seconds, the change is applied, and the result is normalised back to a 12- or 24-hour clock, tracking day rollover.

2. 02

 Measure across midnight

 if end < start: end += 24h

 When an end time is earlier than the start, the calculator can treat it as the next day, so 11:00 PM to 2:30 AM reads 3h 30m.

3. 03

 Convert to payroll hours

 paid = out − in − break · decimal = minutes ÷ 60

 Thirty minutes is 0.5 hours, forty-five is 0.75. Every work-hour result shows both clock and decimal formats.

4. 04

 Walk the calendar

 Date math applies month lengths and leap years correctly rather than assuming 30-day months, and reports the day of week for the result.

Does it handle overnight shifts?

Is there a mobile app or API?

chunks.title: ChatGPT SEO and Perplexity Optimization
chunks.heading: ChatGPT SEO and Perplexity Optimization > ChatGPT SEO for brands that want to show up in AI answers. > ChatGPT SEO questions > How does ChatGPT search find sources?
chunks.text: ChatGPT search sends queries to third-party search providers, including Microsoft Bing, and uses OpenAI's OAI-SearchBot crawler to read pages. It then summarizes what it finds and links the sources it relied on. Pages blocked in robots.txt, missing from Bing's index or hard to render are less likely to be read or cited.

chunks.title: ChatGPT SEO and Perplexity Optimization

chunks.title: ChatGPT SEO and Perplexity Optimization

What we can control is whether your pages are crawlable, clear, consistent and worth citing, and we measure progress on a fixed prompt set instead of promising placements.

chunks.title: CRM Integration Services: HubSpot, Salesforce
chunks.heading: CRM Integration Services: HubSpot, Salesforce > CRM integration services that connect marketing to revenue. > CRM integration questions > How do you pass UTM data and click IDs into the CRM?
chunks.text: We capture UTM parameters, click IDs such as GCLID and FBCLID, the landing page and the referrer when a visitor arrives, store them in first-party cookies and write them into hidden form fields. When the form is submitted, the CRM saves them on the contact and the deal. Reports can then show which campaign produced each lead, opportunity and closed deal.

chunks.title: CRM Integration Services: HubSpot, Salesforce
chunks.heading: CRM Integration Services: HubSpot, Salesforce > CRM integration services that connect marketing to revenue. > CRM integration questions > What are offline conversion imports?
chunks.text: Offline conversion imports send results that happen after the form fill, such as a qualified lead or a closed deal, back to the ad platforms. Google Ads matches them by click ID or enhanced conversions data, and Meta receives them through the Conversions API. Bidding can then optimize toward leads that turn into revenue instead of every form submission.

chunks.title: CRM Integration Services: HubSpot, Salesforce
chunks.heading: CRM Integration Services: HubSpot, Salesforce > CRM integration services that connect marketing to revenue. > CRM integration questions > Can you sync Shopify customers and orders to HubSpot or Salesforce?
chunks.text: Yes. We sync Shopify customers, orders and products to HubSpot with its Shopify integration or to Salesforce with a connector or middleware, then map fields and lifecycle stages. Sales and service teams see order history on each record, and marketing can segment by purchase behavior. We test duplicates and edge cases such as guest checkouts before switching it on.

chunks.title: CRM Integration Services: HubSpot, Salesforce
chunks.heading: CRM Integration Services: HubSpot, Salesforce > CRM integration services that connect marketing to revenue. > CRM integration questions > How do you keep CRM data clean?
chunks.text:
We keep CRM data clean with rules at the point of entry and regular checks. That means required fields, standard values for sources and stages, deduplication by email and company domain, and naming rules for properties. We also audit the CRM every month for duplicates, empty fields and broken integrations, and fix issues before they reach reports.

FAQ

Digital PR is the practice of earning online coverage for a brand through stories that publications want to run. It uses data studies, expert commentary and useful tools as the source of the story. Each piece of coverage can bring a link, a brand mention and referral traffic, which supports search rankings and AI search visibility.

chunks.title: Digital PR Agency for Links and Citations
chunks.heading: Digital PR Agency for Links and Citations > Digital PR agency for earned coverage, links and citations. > Digital PR questions > Is digital PR the same as link building?
chunks.text: Not exactly. Digital PR is one way to build links: it earns them through editorial coverage instead of asking site owners for links one at a time. Questions

Dropship automation is the set of integrations that move inventory, orders and tracking between your store and the suppliers who ship for you. Supplier stock syncs into the store, each order goes to the right supplier without manual entry, and tracking comes back to the customer. It replaces spreadsheets, emailed orders and copy-pasted tracking numbers.

chunks.title: Dropship Automation for Suppliers
chunks.heading: Dropship Automation for Suppliers > Dropship automation for supplier inventory and orders. > Dropship automation questions > How often should supplier inventory sync?
chunks.text: Inventory should sync as often as the supplier can provide reliable data, and fast-moving items need it most. Supplier APIs can usually be checked often, while SFTP and CSV feeds update on the supplier's own schedule. We set a schedule per supplier and can hold back a buffer on low-stock items so the store does not oversell between updates.

chunks.title: Dropship Automation for Suppliers
chunks.heading: Dropship Automation for Suppliers > Dropship automation for supplier inventory and orders. > Dropship automation questions > How do you handle products sold by more than one supplier?
chunks.text: Products sold by more than one supplier are mapped to a single listing, with each supplier's SKU, cost and stock attached. Routing rules then pick the supplier for each order, for example by stock on hand, cost or ship-from location. Customers see one product, and your team sees which supplier filled each order.

chunks.title: Dropship Automation for Suppliers
chunks.heading: Dropship Automation for Suppliers > Dropship automation for supplier inventory and orders. > Dropship automation questions > What happens with backorders and discontinued items?
chunks.text: Backordered and discontinued items are handled by rules you approve. When a supplier marks an item backordered, the store can hide it, show an expected date or route the order to another supplier. Discontinued items are unpublished or redirected so customers and search engines are not sent to dead pages, and every change is logged for your team.

chunks.title: Dropship Automation for Suppliers
chunks.heading: Dropship Automation for Suppliers > Dropship automation for supplier inventory and orders. > Dropship automation questions > Do I need EDI for dropship automation?
chunks.text:
No. Most dropship automation runs on supplier APIs or SFTP and CSV feeds. EDI is needed when a supplier or retail partner requires it, which some larger suppliers do. We connect whatever each supplier supports and bring every supplier into one flow, and our X12 EDI integration service covers the partners that require standard documents.

Questions

EDI, or electronic data interchange, is a set of standard documents that lets your store and a supplier exchange inventory, purchase orders, ship notices and invoices without manual entry. Both sides send and receive the same formats, so orders and updates move automatically instead of by email or spreadsheet.

chunks.title: EDI Integration for Shopify and Ecommerce
chunks.heading: EDI Integration for Shopify and Ecommerce > EDI integration that connects your store and suppliers. > EDI integration questions > Which documents do you set up?
chunks.text: We usually set up inventory updates (846), purchase orders (850), order acknowledgments (855), ship notices (856) and invoices (810). The exact set depends on what each supplier supports. We document every flow so your team knows which supplier sends what and when.

chunks.title: EDI Integration for Shopify and Ecommerce
chunks.heading: EDI Integration for Shopify and Ecommerce > EDI integration that connects your store and suppliers. > EDI integration questions > What if a supplier does not support EDI?
chunks.text: We connect through their API, an SFTP file feed or a scheduled CSV instead. Every supplier ends up in the same automated flow, so your store sees one consistent stream of stock levels, order confirmations and tracking, whatever format each supplier uses.

chunks.title: EDI Integration for Shopify and Ecommerce
chunks.heading: EDI Integration for Shopify and Ecommerce > EDI integration that connects your store and suppliers. > EDI integration questions > Which platforms do you work on?
chunks.text: We work on Shopify stores connected to wholesale and dropship suppliers. That includes custom apps and middleware that sit between Shopify and each trading partner. If you are moving to Shopify from another platform, we plan the EDI connections as part of the migration.

chunks.title: EDI Integration for Shopify and Ecommerce
chunks.heading: EDI Integration for Shopify and Ecommerce > EDI integration that connects your store and suppliers. > EDI integration questions > How do you measure success?
chunks.text:

GA4 is the analytics tool that stores and reports your data, and Google Tag Manager is the tool that sends data to it. If you run Google Ads or have visitors from regions with consent rules, such as the European Economic Area, it needs to be set up correctly. We connect it to your consent tool and test each consent state.

Google Merchant Center is the account that holds your product feed and makes products eligible for Shopping ads and free listings. chunks.title: International SEO Agency for Global Brands
chunks.heading: International SEO Agency for Global Brands > International SEO agency for brands going global. > International SEO questions > What is hreflang?
chunks.text: Hreflang is a tag that tells search engines which language and country each version of a page is for, so they show the right one to each searcher. It has to be set on every version and point both ways to work. Missing or one-way tags are one of the most common international SEO errors.

chunks.title: International SEO Agency for Global Brands
chunks.heading: International SEO Agency for Global Brands > International SEO agency for brands going global. > International SEO questions > Is translating our site enough?

URLs and redirects

chunks.title: Magento to Shopify Migration Services
chunks.heading: Magento to Shopify Migration Services > Magento to Shopify migration, planned around your SEO and data. > How do Magento URLs map to Shopify?
chunks.text:
Magento URLs map to Shopify's fixed /products/, /collections/, /pages/ and /blogs/ paths, so almost every URL changes and needs a 301 redirect. Magento lets you set any URL key and suffix; Shopify does not.

Product pages: /blue-jacket.html or /men/jackets/blue-jacket.html becomes /products/blue-jacket. Each category path version of a product URL gets its own redirect.

chunks.title: Magento to Shopify Migration Services
chunks.heading: Magento to Shopify Migration Services > Magento to Shopify migration, planned around your SEO and data. > How do Magento URLs map to Shopify? > Category pages
chunks.text:
/men/jackets.html becomes /collections/mens-jackets. Shopify collections are flat, so nested categories need a menu and filter plan.

/about-us becomes /pages/about-us. Posts from a Magento blog extension move to Shopify blogs at /blogs/news/post-handle.

All Shopify migrations →

Store view URLs for other countries or languages map to Shopify Markets. Layered navigation filter URLs redirect to the parent collection, not one by one.

chunks.title: Magento to Shopify Migration Services
chunks.heading: Magento to Shopify Migration Services > Magento to Shopify migration, planned around your SEO and data. > Questions about Magento to Shopify migration > Can you migrate Adobe Commerce and Magento 1 stores?
chunks.text: Yes. We migrate Magento 2, Adobe Commerce and Adobe Commerce Cloud stores, and Magento 1 stores still running after Magento 1 reached end of life in June 2020. The data model is similar across versions, so the work is mapping products, attributes, customers and URLs to Shopify, then replacing extensions and integrations.

chunks.title: Magento to Shopify Migration Services
chunks.heading: Magento to Shopify Migration Services > Magento to Shopify migration, planned around your SEO and data. > Questions about Magento to Shopify migration > What happens to configurable products and custom attributes?
chunks.text: Configurable products become Shopify products with variants, and each child simple product becomes a variant with its own SKU, price and inventory. Shopify allows three options per product, so products with more option attributes need a different structure or an options app. Custom attributes used for specs or filters move to metafields.

chunks.title: Magento to Shopify Migration Services
chunks.heading: Magento to Shopify Migration Services > Magento to Shopify migration, planned around your SEO and data. > Questions about Magento to Shopify migration > Can customers keep their accounts and order history?
chunks.text: Customer records, addresses and order history can move from Magento to Shopify, but passwords cannot be migrated for security reasons. After launch, customers receive an account invitation so they can set a new password. We import historical orders for reference and reporting and check totals on a staging store first.

chunks.title: Magento to Shopify Migration Services
chunks.heading: Magento to Shopify Migration Services > Magento to Shopify migration, planned around your SEO and data. > Questions about Magento to Shopify migration > Does Shopify support Magento B2B features and store views?
chunks.text: Largely, through Shopify Plus. Shopify Plus B2B covers company accounts, catalogs with custom pricing, payment terms and quantity rules, which replaces many Adobe Commerce B2B setups. Store views for other countries or languages usually map to Shopify Markets. Features such as requisition lists or complex quote flows may need an app or custom work.

chunks.heading: Magento to Shopify Migration Services > Magento to Shopify migration, planned around your SEO and data. > Questions about Magento to Shopify migration > What happens to our ERP and EDI integrations?
chunks.text:
We rebuild them for Shopify before launch. Common ERPs and EDI providers have Shopify connectors, and others can use the Shopify Admin API. We test product, inventory and order flows against the staging store, plan switch-over day so orders keep flowing to your ERP and suppliers, and watch the feeds closely in the weeks after.

chunks.title: Marketplace Management: Amazon, Walmart, eBay

chunks.text: The Buy Box is the Add to Cart section on an Amazon product page, and the seller who holds it gets the sale when a shopper clicks Add to Cart. chunks.text:
A schema markup audit checks these five things in order, because valid markup only helps when it is also accurate.

1. Is the markup valid? JSON-LD syntax, required and recommended properties, and errors in the Rich Results Test.
2. Does it match the page? Prices, availability, ratings and FAQ text must match what visitors see.
3. Are entities connected? One Organization @id, sameAs links to real profiles, and the same name, address and phone everywhere.
4. Is it eligible? Which rich results Google still shows for your types, and which no longer apply.
5. Does it hold after releases? Search Console enhancement reports and spot checks after theme or CMS changes.

FAQ

Schema markup is structured data, usually written as JSON-LD, that describes a page using the Schema.org vocabulary shared by the major search engines. It tells Google, Bing and AI answer engines exactly what a page is about, such as a product with a price, a service, an article or a business with an address, instead of leaving them to infer it from the text.

chunks.title: Schema Markup Services: Structured Data
chunks.heading: Schema Markup Services: Structured Data > Schema markup services that make your pages machine-readable. > Questions about schema markup > Does schema markup improve rankings?
chunks.text: Schema markup is not a direct ranking factor, according to Google. It helps search engines understand your pages and can make them eligible for rich results such as product prices, review stars and breadcrumbs, which change how your listing looks in search. Eligibility does not guarantee a rich result: Google decides when to show one.

chunks.title: Schema Markup Services: Structured Data
chunks.heading: Schema Markup Services: Structured Data > Schema markup services that make your pages machine-readable. > Questions about schema markup > Which schema types should my site use?
chunks.text: Most sites need Organization or LocalBusiness, BreadcrumbList on inner pages, and one type per template: Product and Offer for product pages, Service for service pages and Article for posts. FAQPage fits pages with a visible FAQ. Review and AggregateRating belong only on pages that show genuine reviews and follow Google's review snippet guidelines.

chunks.title: Schema Markup Services: Structured Data
chunks.heading: Schema Markup Services: Structured Data > Schema markup services that make your pages machine-readable. > Questions about schema markup > How do you add schema markup on Shopify, Webflow or WordPress?
chunks.text: We add JSON-LD to templates rather than page by page. On Shopify that means Liquid theme sections that pull product, price and availability data. On Webflow we use page and CMS template custom code bound to CMS fields. On WordPress we configure an SEO plugin or write theme code. Every template is validated before release.

chunks.title: Schema Markup Services: Structured Data
chunks.heading: Schema Markup Services: Structured Data > Schema markup services that make your pages machine-readable. > Questions about schema markup > Does structured data help with AI search?
chunks.text:
Yes, structured data helps AI answer engines read your entity facts consistently: your business name, services, products and locations. Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity still decide what to cite on their own, so schema works alongside clear, crawlable content and consistent facts across the web. We treat it as one input, not a guarantee of citations.

Server-side tracking sends conversion events from a server you control to analytics and ad platforms, instead of relying only on scripts in the visitor's browser. A server-side Google Tag Manager container or a platform conversions API receives each event, adds the details the platform needs and forwards it. Ad blockers and browser limits affect it less, and you control what data is shared.

chunks.title: Server-Side Tracking and Conversions API Setup
chunks.heading: Server-Side Tracking and Conversions API Setup > Server-side tracking that gets conversion data back to your ad platforms. > Server-side tracking questions > Why do browser pixels miss conversions?
chunks.text: Browser pixels miss conversions because ad blockers stop them from loading, browsers such as Safari limit cookies and click identifiers, and visitors who decline consent are not tracked. Checkouts on other domains and slow pages drop events too. Meta, Google Ads and TikTok then see fewer conversions than really happened, which weakens their bidding and makes campaigns look worse than they are.

chunks.title: Server-Side Tracking and Conversions API Setup
chunks.heading: Server-Side Tracking and Conversions API Setup > Server-side tracking that gets conversion data back to your ad platforms. > Server-side tracking questions > What is the Meta Conversions API and do we need it?
chunks.text: The Meta Conversions API sends events such as purchases and leads from your server directly to Meta. Most brands running Facebook and Instagram ads benefit from it, because it recovers events the Meta Pixel misses and improves event match quality. We run it alongside the pixel with shared event IDs, so Meta counts each conversion once.

chunks.title: Server-Side Tracking and Conversions API Setup
chunks.heading: Server-Side Tracking and Conversions API Setup > Server-side tracking that gets conversion data back to your ad platforms. > Server-side tracking questions > How do you avoid double counting conversions?
chunks.text: We avoid double counting with deduplication. Each conversion gets one event ID that is sent with both the browser event and the server event, and platforms such as Meta and TikTok use it to keep only one. For Google Ads we use enhanced conversions with transaction IDs. We then compare platform numbers with orders or CRM leads to confirm the counts line up.

chunks.title: Server-Side Tracking and Conversions API Setup
chunks.heading: Server-Side Tracking and Conversions API Setup > Server-side tracking that gets conversion data back to your ad platforms. > Server-side tracking questions > Does server-side tracking work with Shopify?
chunks.text:
Yes. On Shopify we use customer events and web pixels, which work with Checkout Extensibility, and send events to a server-side Google Tag Manager container or straight to platform APIs. The Meta and Google sales channel apps for Shopify also send server events, so we check what they already cover before adding anything, to avoid duplicates.

A brand usually needs Shopify Plus when it needs what standard plans limit or leave out: the full B2B feature set, checkout customization across every step, custom apps built on Shopify Functions, expansion stores, Launchpad, or higher API limits for ERP and 3PL integrations. chunks.title: Shopify Plus Agency for Growing Brands
chunks.heading: Shopify Plus Agency for Growing Brands > A Shopify Plus agency for brands that have outgrown standard Shopify. > Questions about Shopify Plus > What replaced checkout.liquid on Shopify Plus?
chunks.text: Checkout Extensibility replaced checkout.liquid. Shopify has deprecated checkout.liquid, so checkout customizations now use checkout UI extensions, Shopify Functions for discount, shipping and payment logic, checkout branding settings and web pixels for tracking. We audit what your current checkout does, rebuild each customization in the supported model and test it in a development store before switching over.

chunks.title: Shopify Plus Agency for Growing Brands
chunks.heading: Shopify Plus Agency for Growing Brands > A Shopify Plus agency for brands that have outgrown standard Shopify. > Questions about Shopify Plus > Can Shopify Plus handle B2B and wholesale?
chunks.text: Yes. Shopify Plus includes B2B features: company accounts with multiple buyers and locations, catalogs and price lists, payment terms, quantity rules and draft orders. Wholesale buyers can order from the same store as retail customers or from a separate expansion store. We set up the B2B configuration and connect it to your ERP so pricing and orders stay in sync.

chunks.heading: Shopify Plus Agency for Growing Brands > A Shopify Plus agency for brands that have outgrown standard Shopify. > Questions about Shopify Plus > Can you migrate our store to Shopify Plus?
chunks.text: Yes. We migrate stores from Magento, BigCommerce, WooCommerce and Salesforce Commerce Cloud, and upgrade standard Shopify stores to Plus. Products, customers, orders and content move over, every URL gets a 301 redirect and SEO elements carry across, all planned to protect search traffic. Our Magento to Shopify migration page covers the process in detail.

chunks.title: Shopify Plus Agency for Growing Brands
chunks.heading: Shopify Plus Agency for Growing Brands > A Shopify Plus agency for brands that have outgrown standard Shopify. > Questions about Shopify Plus > Do you connect Shopify Plus to ERP, 3PL and EDI systems?
chunks.text:
Yes. We connect Shopify Plus to ERPs such as NetSuite, to 3PL warehouses and to retail partners over EDI, so orders, inventory, shipments and invoices move without manual entry. We use the Shopify Admin API, webhooks and middleware where it fits, and we monitor the connections after launch so failed syncs are caught and fixed quickly.

chunks.title: Shopify SEO Agency: Collection Architecture
chunks.heading: Shopify SEO Agency: Collection Architecture > Shopify SEO for stores at catalog scale. > Shopify SEO questions > Does this work with AI answer engines?

chunks.title: Site Speed Optimization Services
chunks.heading: Site Speed Optimization Services > Site speed optimization built around Core Web Vitals. > How does Google measure site speed?
chunks.text:
Google measures site speed with field data from real Chrome users in the Chrome UX Report (CrUX), and assesses Core Web Vitals at the 75th percentile of page visits.

1. Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): how long the main image or text block takes to appear.
2. Interaction to Next Paint (INP): how quickly the page responds to taps, clicks and key presses.
3. Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): how much the layout jumps while the page loads.
4. Field data: real-user CrUX results shown in Search Console and PageSpeed Insights over a rolling 28-day window.
5. Lab data: Lighthouse tests run in a controlled setting, useful for debugging but not what Google uses to assess Core Web Vitals.

chunks.text: They often show different data. The PageSpeed Insights performance score comes from a single Lighthouse lab test on a simulated device. /about/ becomes /pages/about, and a post at /post-name/ becomes /blogs/news/post-name if the blog moves to Shopify.

What’s included

chunks.title: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce
chunks.heading: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce > X12 EDI integration for ecommerce brands and retailers. > What is X12 EDI?
chunks.text:
X12 EDI is the ANSI standard format that North American retailers, suppliers and logistics providers use to exchange business documents. Each document type is a numbered transaction set, such as the 850 purchase order. These are the sets ecommerce brands and retailers exchange most.

01

chunks.title: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce
chunks.heading: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce > X12 EDI integration for ecommerce brands and retailers. > What is X12 EDI? > 850 and 855: orders
chunks.text:
The 850 purchase order says what a partner wants to buy. The 855 PO acknowledgment confirms what you accept, change or reject.

02

The 856 ASN lists the cartons, items and tracking in each shipment, matched to the GS1-128 carton labels many retailers require.

03

chunks.title: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce
chunks.heading: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce > X12 EDI integration for ecommerce brands and retailers. > What is X12 EDI? > 810: invoice
chunks.text:
The 810 bills each order in the partner's format, checked against the 850 and 856 so quantities and totals reconcile.

04

The 846 shares stock levels with a partner on a schedule, so retailers and marketplaces only sell what can ship.

05

chunks.title: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce
chunks.heading: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce > X12 EDI integration for ecommerce brands and retailers. > What is X12 EDI? > 940 and 945: warehouse orders
chunks.text:
The 940 warehouse shipping order tells a 3PL what to ship. The 945 warehouse shipping advice confirms what actually shipped.

06

The 997 confirms each document arrived and passed syntax checks. A rejected 997 is the first sign that something failed.

How we run it

chunks.title: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce
chunks.heading: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce > X12 EDI integration for ecommerce brands and retailers. > How does X12 EDI onboarding with a trading partner work?
chunks.text:
X12 EDI onboarding works in four steps: collect the partner's requirements, connect and map, test with the partner, then go live with monitoring. Most retail partners will not accept live documents until test documents pass their checks.

If a partner does not require X12, a supplier API or CSV feed is often the better fit. See dropship automation or the wider EDI and ecommerce operations service.

01

chunks.title: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce
chunks.heading: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce > X12 EDI integration for ecommerce brands and retailers. > How does X12 EDI onboarding with a trading partner work? > Requirements
chunks.text:
Collect each partner's implementation guide: transaction sets, X12 version, IDs, label rules and communication method.

02

Set up AS2, SFTP or a VAN mailbox, then map each X12 segment to Shopify or ERP fields such as SKU, UPC and ship-to.

03

chunks.title: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce
chunks.heading: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce > X12 EDI integration for ecommerce brands and retailers. > How does X12 EDI onboarding with a trading partner work? > Test with the partner
chunks.text:
Exchange test 850, 855, 856 and 810 documents until each one passes the partner's compliance checks.

04

Switch to production with alerts for rejected 997s, failed maps and late ASNs, each with a named owner.

Questions

Most ecommerce brands that sell to retailers need the 850 purchase order, 855 PO acknowledgment, 856 advance ship notice, 810 invoice and 997 functional acknowledgment. Dropship and inventory programs add the 846, and brands that ship through a 3PL add the 940 and 945. The exact list comes from each trading partner's implementation guide, so we confirm it before mapping starts.

chunks.title: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce
chunks.heading: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce > X12 EDI integration for ecommerce brands and retailers. > X12 EDI questions > What is the difference between AS2, SFTP and a VAN?
chunks.text: AS2 sends EDI files directly between two partners over the internet, encrypted and with signed receipts. SFTP moves files through a secure server that one side hosts and the other polls. A VAN, or value-added network, is a third-party mailbox service that routes documents between many partners. The trading partner usually decides which method you use, and we set up whichever one they require.

chunks.title: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce
chunks.heading: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce > X12 EDI integration for ecommerce brands and retailers. > X12 EDI questions > How is X12 EDI mapped to Shopify or an ERP?
chunks.text: Each X12 segment is mapped to a field in Shopify or your ERP. The PO number, ship-to address, SKU or UPC, quantity and price on an 850 become an order, and fulfillment data becomes the 856 and 810. We use an EDI translator or middleware for the conversion and document every mapping rule, so product or partner changes do not quietly break the flow.

chunks.title: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce
chunks.heading: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce > X12 EDI integration for ecommerce brands and retailers. > X12 EDI questions > What happens when an EDI document fails?
chunks.text: A failed document is flagged as soon as a 997 comes back rejected, a map throws an error or an expected document does not arrive. The alert goes to a named owner with the partner, PO number and reason, so the issue is fixed and resent before it turns into a late shipment, a chargeback or a missed payment.

chunks.title: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce
chunks.heading: X12 EDI Integration for Ecommerce > X12 EDI integration for ecommerce brands and retailers. > X12 EDI questions > When is an API or CSV feed better than X12 EDI?
chunks.text:
An API or CSV feed is often the better fit when the partner does not require EDI, which is common with dropship and wholesale suppliers. These feeds are faster to set up and easier to change. X12 EDI is the right choice when a retailer, marketplace or 3PL requires it, or when a standard format across many partners is worth the setup.

Costume sizes vary by brand, so every product page carries its own sizing help: how sizes work, what to check before ordering, and how to measure chest, waist, hips, height, inseam and head. Shipping and returns answers sit on the same page.

chunks.title: Spooky Costumes Case Study: Shopify and EDI
chunks.heading: Spooky Costumes Case Study: Shopify and EDI > A Shopify store built for 8,000 costumes and one deadline. > How does supplier EDI work for the store?
chunks.text: Behind the storefront, we built EDI connections to the costume suppliers. Inventory flows into the store automatically and each order routes to the supplier that holds the stock, so shoppers see what is really available in peak season. Seasonal messaging on the front end, from the Halloween date to ship times and expedited checkout, tells them what will arrive in time.
